questions.stem: When sodium (Na) forms an ionic bond with chlorine (Cl), what happens to the electrons?

options.text: Chlorine transfers one electron to sodium
Sodium and chlorine share a pair of electrons
Both atoms lose electrons to form positive ions
Sodium transfers one electron to chlorine

questions.explanation: Sodium has 1 electron in its outer shell (2,8,1) which it transfers to chlorine. This gives sodium a full outer shell (2,8) forming Na+, and chlorine gains the electron to achieve a full outer shell (2,8,8) forming Cl-.
